route_notes.note: Approve with three changes; keep everything else as it is. (1) Neon driver: use Drizzle's neon-serverless driver (a Pool from @neondatabase/serverless over WebSocket) when DATABASE_URL is set, not the http driver. The http driver cannot hold an interactive transaction, and creating, editing or deleting an expense must write the expense, its payers, its shares and its activity entry atomically (TR-8: never half-written). Update ADR-0002, the getDb() interface, and TR-2's proof: the Neon smoke test runs one transaction that rolls back on error and leaves nothing behind. (2) Store the split rule with the expense, not only its result: the split type on Expense, and on each split line the member's input as entered (exact amount, percentage or share count, and whether they were included) beside the computed share. The edit form reopens showing exactly what was entered. Balances still read only the stored payer parts and computed shares. Add it to the data model, the expense editor in docs/ui.md, and an ADR. (3) The spec says every change is recorded 'with who made it and what changed': an expense-edited activity entry stores a structured before/after of the fields that changed (description, amount, date, payers, participants, split type and inputs, category, note), written in the same transaction as the edit. Say so in TR-10 and the ActivityEvent model.

All three changes are in; thank you. One addition, then I approve: the Pool's lifecycle on Vercel. A WebSocket Pool must not outlive the request that uses it on serverless (Neon's guidance for @neondatabase/serverless): getDb() on the Neon side opens the Pool for the request and closes it when the request's work is done, including after an error, and nothing holds a Pool or client at module scope. Say this in the getDb() interface in docs/trd.md and in ADR-0002. And since CI and QA run on PGlite only, add an invariant that no code may branch on which backend it is running against except getDb() itself, so a Neon-only code path cannot hide from the tests. Keep everything else as it is.

breakdown.understanding: Epic #1 is greenfield Tabs (the repo has no code): the PRD order is skeleton and accounts first, groups and members second, expenses third, balances and settle-up fourth, activity plus seed and deploy guide last, and the two human replan-project decisions (neon-serverless WebSocket Pool opened and closed per request including on error with nothing at module scope; split rule stored as split type plus per-line inputs beside computed shares with balances reading only stored parts and shares; expense-edited entries carrying a structured before and after written in the same transaction; no backend branching outside getDb()) bind every piece and already live in project.md and docs/trd.md. issues.json holds only #1 itself as sdlc:epic with pulls and closed empty and no roadmap, so there is no other epic to depend on and no epic_links. Six vertical slices chained 1 to 6, each plannable, buildable, reviewable and QA-able in a browser. Clubbing test against a rough 6-file single-PR budget, one line per adjacent pair: [1-2] skeleton versus accounts: low file overlap (app shell, getDb, migrations and health versus lib/auth plus auth screens), accounts independently demoable as signup to profile, combined infra-plus-security too big for one review, so SPLIT. [2-3] accounts versus groups: new surface (group and membership schema, invite and placeholder flow, membership-first authz pattern), groups demoable without any expense (create, invite, claim, rotate, archive), combined identity-plus-boundary too big, so SPLIT. [3-4] groups versus expenses: partial screen overlap on group detail but genuinely new domain (money calculators, four split inputs, multi-payer sums, interactive transactions); expenses meaningless without groups while groups stand alone, and combined membership-plus-ledger would overflow one work order, so SPLIT; the tempting sub-split of piece 4 by split type (equal, exact, percentage, shares) is REJECTED and clubbed inside piece 4 because the later types touch the same calculators and editor inputs, have no standalone value without expense create and list, and all four plus multi-payer fit one PR with two acceptance groups (base create and list, variant inputs and atomicity). [4-5] expenses versus balances: different modules and screens (lib/money and editor versus lib/settle, debts card, home totals and payments); balances are the payoff users trust once a ledger exists, and ledger writes plus derivation plus payments together exceed one PR, so SPLIT. [5-6] balances versus activity, seed and docs: different modules (settle and payments versus activity readers, seed script and README); a feed without payments still shows expense and member events but settle without a feed is already the trusted-numbers payoff, and simplification plus full audit plus seed plus deploy docs would overflow one review, so SPLIT; the tempting sub-splits inside piece 6 by event kind (expense versus payment versus member rows) and a standalone seed-docs issue are REJECTED and clubbed because they share the same writer path and feed UI, one event kind alone is not demoable history, and feed plus seed plus README still fit one work order.
